Chapter 11: Rethinking Education and Work—Creating Space for Range
So, if the world actually rewards people who have a broad set of skills, why do so many of our schools, businesses, and even families keep pushing us to specialize early on? It’s a question that’s more relevant than ever, especially as the world keeps changing around us.
Picture this: a classroom where students are encouraged to explore lots of different subjects, to follow their curiosity, and to make connections between things that don’t always seem related at first. Instead of funneling kids into one narrow track, the focus is on helping them build resilience—and the kind of curiosity that makes them want to keep learning, even when things get tough.
And here’s the interesting part: the students who really thrive in that environment aren’t always the ones who get perfect scores on every test. They’re the ones who ask the big questions, who try new things, and who aren’t afraid to stumble or fail along the way.
The book shares some great examples of organizations that have embraced this idea of range. For instance, some companies actually rotate their employees through different roles, letting them pick up new skills and see the business from all kinds of perspectives. Others encourage people to work on side projects, or to join teams made up of folks from different backgrounds. The result? Workforces that are more creative, more adaptable, and way better at dealing with change.
Most of us don’t realize just how much flexibility there is to rethink the way we learn and work. Those old systems that pressure people to specialize early—they’re often built on assumptions that just don’t hold up anymore. In a world that’s moving this fast, what really matters is being able to adapt, to keep learning, and to connect ideas in new ways.
So, what’s the best way to get ready for whatever’s coming next? It’s all about making space for range. That means encouraging exploration, rewarding curiosity, and recognizing the value of having a broad skill set—not just being an expert in one thing.
